root_cause.text: In `drivers/crypto/ccp/sev-dev.c`’s `sev_ioctl_do_get_id2()`, the code copied the firmware-reported ID blob to userspace even when the PSP/firmware command failed, so an invalid-length error could make it use a length larger than the kernel-allocated buffer and overread/leak memory.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (ret || WARN_ON_ONCE(argp->error)) goto e_free;` before `copy_to_user(input_address, id_blob, data.len)`, and the CVE description says that when the firmware command failed due to invalid length, “copying the number of bytes _firmware_ requires will overflow the kernel-allocated buffer and leak data to userspace,” with KASAN reporting a slab-out-of-bounds read in `sev_ioctl_do_get_id2()` at the `copy_to_user()` call.

intent_record.intent_summary: Abort SEV ID2 handling on prior errors or unexpected error state before copying the response to user space.
intent_record.what: A new conditional check was inserted after the previous operation and before the `id_blob` handling: `if (ret || WARN_ON_ONCE(argp->error)) goto e_free;`.
intent_record.how: This causes the function to stop and free resources immediately if the prior call failed (`ret` is nonzero) or if `argp->error` is unexpectedly set, preventing the code from continuing into the user-copy path with an invalid or failed state.

grouping_result.intent: Abort SEV ID2 handling on prior errors or unexpected error state before copying the response to user space.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds an early abort before copying the SEV ID2 response to userspace when an error state is present, preventing the unsafe copy that could use an invalid length and overread memory.

candidates.rationale: This is the user-copy site that uses the firmware-reported length. If the prior PSP/firmware command failed or returned an invalid length, copying `data.len` bytes can overread past the allocated kernel buffer and leak memory to userspace.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement copies the firmware-reported ID blob to userspace using data.len even when the prior PSP/firmware command failed or returned an invalid length. That can make the kernel read beyond the allocated buffer and leak memory.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is present in `sev_ioctl_do_get_id2()`: after `ret = __sev_do_cmd_locked(SEV_CMD_GET_ID, &data, &argp->error);`, the code unconditionally uses firmware-populated `data.len` and then copies `id_blob` to userspace with `copy_to_user(input_address, id_blob, data.len)`. The root cause says the firmware command could fail with an invalid-length error and still leave a length larger than the kernel-allocated buffer, causing an overread/leak. This snippet shows no check of `ret` or `argp->error` before using `data.len`, so the vulnerable construct is present. The fix is not present here because there is no validation that the command succeeded before returning/copying the buffer length; it still copies based on `data.len` even on failure.
